# MilPayTools
> Free military pay and benefits calculators built on official 2026 DoD and VA data. No account required. No personal information collected. Calculations run in the browser.

## Calculators (16)
- [Total Military Compensation](/calculators/total-compensation): Full pay breakdown with BAH, BAS, tax advantages, TSP match, TRICARE healthcare value, and civilian salary equivalent — including what a civilian would need to earn to match your total package
- [BAH Calculator](/calculators/bah): 2026 BAH rates for all 40,959 ZIP codes
- [VA Disability Rating](/calculators/va-disability): Combined rating calculator with bilateral factor and 2026 compensation rates
- [TSP Growth Projector](/calculators/tsp): Retirement savings projections with fund allocation
- [Military Retirement](/calculators/retirement): High-3 and BRS pension projections with lifetime value
- [PCS Cost Estimator](/calculators/pcs): DLA, MALT, per diem, TLE, and PPM profit estimates
- [Guard/Reserve Pay](/calculators/guard-reserve): Drill pay, annual training, and TRICARE Reserve Select
- [Education Benefits](/calculators/education): GI Bill vs VR&E vs TA comparison by school
- [CONUS COLA](/calculators/cola): Cost of living allowance lookup by ZIP
- [Duty Station Comparison](/calculators/compare): Side-by-side BAH, taxes, COLA, and take-home
- [Deployment Pay](/calculators/deployment): Combat zone tax exclusion and special pays
- [2026 Pay Charts](/calculators/pay-charts): Full pay tables for all ranks and years of service
- [Dual Military BAH](/calculators/dual-military-bah): BAH scenarios for military couples
- [Transition Readiness](/calculators/transition-readiness): Am I financially ready to leave the military?
- [Separation Benefits Timeline](/calculators/separation-timeline): When each benefit stops, converts, or expires after separation
- [Healthcare Cost Comparison](/calculators/healthcare-comparison): TRICARE vs civilian healthcare cost comparison

## Guides (7)
- [Starting Service: Military Pay & Benefits from Day One](/guides/starting-service): New service member guide — total compensation, BAH, TSP enrollment, LES, and first-year financial checkpoints
- [Military Pay & Compensation Guide](/guides/military-pay): Understanding base pay, BAH, BAS, tax advantages, and total compensation
- [PCS & Duty Station Financial Guide](/guides/pcs): DLA, MALT, per diem, TLE, PPM, and duty station cost comparison tools
- [VA Disability Benefits Guide](/guides/va-disability): Combined rating formula, bilateral factor, 2026 compensation rates, CRDP and CRSC

- [Military Education Benefits Guide](/guides/education-benefits): GI Bill, VR&E, TA, and Montgomery GI Bill comparison and sequencing strategy
- [Military Transition Financial Roadmap](/transition): Full financial arc of military separation — income, healthcare, benefits, and deadlines

## BAH by Duty Station

- [BAH Rates by Military Installation](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah): Index page with search and filter for all duty station BAH pages. Find any installation by name, city, state, or branch.

- [Fort Liberty (formerly Fort Bragg)](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-liberty): Fayetteville, NC — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the 82nd Airborne Division's home station, the largest U.S. military installation by population.

- [Fort Campbell](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-campbell): Clarksville, TN — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the home of the 101st Airborne Division (Air Assault), straddling the Kentucky-Tennessee border.

- [Fort Cavazos (formerly Fort Hood)](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-cavazos): Killeen, TX — Army. 2026 BAH rates for one of the most affordable large military markets in the country, home to III Armored Corps.

- [Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM)](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/joint-base-lewis-mcchord): Lakewood, WA — Army/Air Force. 2026 BAH rates for the largest military installation on the West Coast; CONUS COLA added for this area in 2026.

- [Fort Carson](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-carson): Colorado Springs, CO — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the home of the 4th Infantry Division at the base of Pikes Peak.

- [Fort Drum](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-drum): Watertown, NY — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the home of the 10th Mountain Division in upstate New York.

- [Fort Bliss](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-bliss): El Paso, TX — Army. 2026 BAH rates for one of the most affordable major housing markets in the country, home to the 1st Armored Division.

- [Fort Stewart](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-stewart): Hinesville, GA — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the largest Army installation east of the Mississippi River, home to the 3rd Infantry Division.

- [Fort Knox](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-knox): Radcliff, KY — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the home of Armor School and the U.S. Army Human Resources Command.

- [Fort Riley](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-riley): Junction City, KS — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the home of the 1st Infantry Division ("Big Red One") in north-central Kansas.

- [Fort Moore (formerly Fort Benning)](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-moore): Columbus, GA — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the Maneuver Center of Excellence and Ranger Training Brigade.

- [Fort Eisenhower (formerly Fort Gordon)](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-eisenhower): Augusta, GA — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the U.S. Army Cyber Center of Excellence and Signal Corps.

- [Fort Sill](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-sill): Lawton, OK — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the home of the Field Artillery School; one of the most affordable military housing markets in the country.

- [Fort Leavenworth](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-leavenworth): Leavenworth, KS — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the Command and General Staff College; falls within the Kansas City MHA.

- [Fort Huachuca](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-huachuca): Sierra Vista, AZ — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the U.S. Army Intelligence Center of Excellence in southeastern Arizona.

- [Fort Wainwright](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-wainwright): Fairbanks, AK — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the coldest major U.S. military installation, home to the 1st Brigade Combat Team (Stryker), 25th Infantry Division.

- [Fort Johnson (formerly Fort Polk)](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-johnson): Leesville, LA — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the Joint Readiness Training Center (JRTC) installation in western Louisiana.

- [Schofield Barracks](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/schofield-barracks): Wahiawa, HI — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the home of the 25th Infantry Division on Oahu; among the highest BAH rates in the DoD.

- [Aberdeen Proving Ground](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/aberdeen-proving-ground): Aberdeen, MD — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the Army's primary research and testing center; falls within the Baltimore MHA.

- [Redstone Arsenal](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/redstone-arsenal): Huntsville, AL — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the Army Aviation and Missile Command center in Huntsville's technology corridor.

- [Fort Hamilton](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-hamilton): Brooklyn, NY — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the only active-duty military installation in New York City; NYC MHA rates apply.

- [Fort Jackson](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-jackson): Columbia, SC — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the Army's largest initial entry training center in the affordable Columbia market.

- [Fort Detrick](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-detrick): Frederick, MD — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command; falls within the DC-area BAH zone.

- [Fort Irwin (National Training Center)](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/fort-irwin): Barstow, CA — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the Army's premier large-scale combat training center in the Mojave Desert.

- [United States Military Academy at West Point](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/west-point): West Point, NY — Army. 2026 BAH rates for the nation's premier military university; falls within the New York City metro MHA.

- [Joint Base San Antonio](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/joint-base-san-antonio): San Antonio, TX — Air Force/Multi-branch. 2026 BAH rates for the largest joint base in the DoD; one of the most affordable large metros in the country.

- [Wright-Patterson AFB](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/wright-patterson-afb): Dayton, OH — Air Force. 2026 BAH rates for Air Force Materiel Command headquarters in Dayton's highly affordable market.

- [Luke AFB](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/luke-afb): Glendale, AZ — Air Force. 2026 BAH rates for the world's largest fighter pilot training base in the western Phoenix metro.

- [Vandenberg Space Force Base](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/vandenberg-sfb): Lompoc, CA — Space Force/Air Force. 2026 BAH rates for the primary West Coast space launch facility; BAH reflects the Santa Barbara MHA.

- [Seymour Johnson AFB](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/seymour-johnson-afb): Goldsboro, NC — Air Force. 2026 BAH rates for the home of the 4th Fighter Wing and F-15E Strike Eagles in eastern North Carolina.

- [Ellsworth AFB](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/ellsworth-afb): Rapid City, SD — Air Force. 2026 BAH rates for the 28th Bomb Wing (B-1B Lancer) near the Black Hills; no state income tax on military pay.

- [Minot AFB](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/minot-afb): Minot, ND — Air Force. 2026 BAH rates for the dual-mission B-52H and ICBM base; one of the most affordable military markets in the country.

- [Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/joint-base-elmendorf-richardson): Anchorage, AK — Air Force/Army. 2026 BAH rates for the primary military installation in Alaska, home to the 3rd Wing and 11th Airborne Division.

- [Joint Base Andrews](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/joint-base-andrews): Camp Springs, MD — Air Force/Army. 2026 BAH rates for the home of Air Force One in the high-cost DC metro MHA.

- [Kirtland AFB](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/kirtland-afb): Albuquerque, NM — Air Force. 2026 BAH rates for the Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center and Sandia National Laboratories in an affordable market.

- [Naval Station Norfolk](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/naval-station-norfolk): Norfolk, VA — Navy. 2026 BAH rates for the largest naval base in the world; Hampton Roads is a major military housing market with competitive rates.

- [Naval Air Station Pensacola](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/naval-air-station-pensacola): Pensacola, FL — Navy. 2026 BAH rates for the "Cradle of Naval Aviation" and Blue Angels home base on the Florida Gulf Coast.

- [Naval Air Station Whidbey Island](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/naval-air-station-whidbey-island): Oak Harbor, WA — Navy. 2026 BAH rates for the EA-18G Growler and P-8 Poseidon base; tied to the Seattle MHA with favorable BAH-to-rent ratio on the island.

- [MCAS Beaufort](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/marine-corps-air-station-beaufort): Beaufort, SC — Marine Corps/Navy. 2026 BAH rates for the F-35B operational base in South Carolina's Lowcountry.

- [Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/joint-base-mcguire-dix-lakehurst): Wrightstown, NJ — Air Force/Army/Navy. 2026 BAH rates for the only U.S. base hosting all three Total Force components; Philadelphia/South Jersey MHA.

- [Naval Air Station Oceana](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/naval-air-station-oceana): Virginia Beach, VA — Navy. 2026 BAH rates for the East Coast Master Jet Base and primary F/A-18 strike fighter training pipeline.

- [MCAGCC Twentynine Palms](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/marine-corps-air-ground-combat-center): Twentynine Palms, CA — Marine Corps. 2026 BAH rates for the world's largest Marine Corps base and combined-arms training center in the Mojave Desert.

- [Joint Base Charleston](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/joint-base-charleston): North Charleston, SC — Air Force/Navy. 2026 BAH rates for the 437th Airlift Wing and primary East Coast port of embarkation.

- [Joint Base Cape Cod](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/joint-base-cape-cod): Bourne, MA — Air Force/Army/Coast Guard. 2026 BAH rates for the multi-service installation on Cape Cod; elevated Massachusetts coastal market rates.

- [Yokota Air Base](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/yokota-air-base): Fussa, Japan — Air Force. OCONUS installation — members receive Overseas Housing Allowance (OHA), not BAH. Headquarters for U.S. Forces Japan in the western Tokyo metropolitan area.

- [Kadena Air Base](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/kadena-air-base): Okinawa, Japan — Air Force/Multi-branch. OCONUS installation — members receive OHA, not BAH. Largest U.S. Air Force base in Asia and keystone of Pacific air defense.

- [Camp Humphreys (K-6)](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/camp-humphreys): Pyeongtaek, South Korea — Army/Air Force. OCONUS installation — members receive OHA, not BAH. Largest U.S. overseas military base in the world and headquarters of U.S. Forces Korea.

- [Ramstein Air Base](https://www.milpaytools.com/bah/ramstein-air-base): Ramstein-Miesenbach, Germany — Air Force/Army. OCONUS installation — members receive OHA, not BAH. Hub of U.S. military operations in Europe and headquarters of USAFE-AFAFRICA.

## Blog

- [How Much Does an E-5 Really Make in 2026?](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/how-much-does-an-e5-really-make-2026): Complete E-5 compensation breakdown including base pay ($3,946.80/month), BAH by location, BAS, tax advantages, and civilian salary equivalent.

- [VA Disability Math Explained](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/va-disability-math-explained): Step-by-step explanation of VA combined rating formula with examples showing why 50% + 30% = 70% (not 80%), bilateral factor, and 2026 compensation rates.

- [2026 BAH Rates Complete Guide](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/bah-rates-2026-complete-guide): Comprehensive guide to 2026 BAH rates including rates for 10 major installations, highest/lowest areas, rate protection rules, and PCS comparison guidance.

- [BRS vs High-3: Which Military Retirement System Is Better?](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/brs-vs-high-3-retirement): Side-by-side comparison of BRS and legacy High-3 retirement, with pension math for E-7 at 20 years, TSP matching value, continuation pay, and break-even analysis.

- [The Roth TSP Advantage Nobody Explains to Junior Enlisted](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/roth-tsp-advantage-junior-enlisted): Why the Roth TSP is the optimal choice for junior enlisted, including combat zone triple tax advantage and long-term compounding math.

- [What Civilian Salary Do I Need After the Military?](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/what-civilian-salary-do-i-need): Step-by-step comparison of military total compensation to civilian salary equivalents by rank, including healthcare replacement and tax-free allowance grossup.

- [Are You Financially Ready to Leave the Military?](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/are-you-financially-ready-to-leave-the-military): Comprehensive guide to the transition readiness decision. Covers the three-factor readiness test (income surplus ≥ $500/month after healthcare replacement, emergency fund ≥ 6 months, VA claim filed or retirement making VA moot), why healthcare is the most underestimated transition cost ($1,400–$2,000/month for a family on the open market vs. $0 on active-duty TRICARE Prime), why TSP doesn't count as emergency fund (10% penalty + ordinary income tax before 59½), and how VA BDD filing before separation can close the income gap from day one. Includes a worked example (E-6, 10 years, JBSA, $75K target salary, 40% VA rating) showing a $374/month surplus — Not Yet verdict due to 2.5-month emergency fund runway.

- [File for VA Disability Before You Separate](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/file-va-disability-before-separation): How the BDD program works, why filing on active duty produces better outcomes, and the lifetime value of VA disability compensation.

- [Military Tax Advantages Most Service Members Miss](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/military-tax-advantages): BAH/BAS exclusions, combat zone tax exclusion, Roth TSP deployment triple advantage, state domicile strategy, and EITC eligibility for junior enlisted.

- [Post-9/11 GI Bill Explained: What It's Actually Worth in 2026](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/post-911-gi-bill-explained-2026): Complete breakdown of GI Bill Chapter 33 — tuition coverage (100% in-state public, $30,908.34/year private cap), monthly housing allowance by ZIP code, books stipend, eligibility tiers by service length, Forever GI Bill expiration rules, and transfer-to-dependents requirements.

- [GI Bill vs Tuition Assistance: Which to Use First](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/gi-bill-vs-tuition-assistance): Strategic guide to sequencing TA and GI Bill — why using GI Bill on active duty wastes the $83,000+ housing allowance, TA limits ($250/credit, $4,500/year), and how to preserve GI Bill months for post-separation use.

- [GI Bill Housing Allowance: Why Your School's ZIP Code Matters More Than Tuition](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/gi-bill-housing-allowance-zip-code): GI Bill MHA equals E-5 with-dependents BAH at the school's ZIP code — ranging from $1,100/month in rural areas to $5,000+/month in high-cost cities. Covers hybrid enrollment rules, August 1 update cycle, and part-time proration.

- [VR&E (Chapter 31) vs GI Bill: The Benefit Most Veterans Don't Know About](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/vre-chapter-31-vs-gi-bill): Veteran Readiness and Employment covers unlimited tuition, full books/equipment, and matching housing allowance — without depleting GI Bill months. Eligibility requires 10%+ VA rating and employment barrier. Includes 48-month combined ceiling and application process.

- [Should I Stay to 20 Years? The Financial Math Behind the Biggest Military Career Decision](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/should-i-stay-to-20-years-military): Full financial analysis of the stay-vs-separate decision — E-7 pension math ($3,059/month High-3, $2,447/month BRS), $2M+ lifetime pension value, zero partial vesting under High-3, healthcare replacement costs ($15,000–$25,000/year), and marginal value of years beyond 20.

- [How BAH Builds Wealth (If You Don't Waste It on Rent)](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/how-bah-builds-wealth): How the BAH surplus gap — the difference between your housing allowance and your actual housing cost — creates a tax-free wealth-building opportunity. Covers BAH arbitrage, VA loan math for moderate-cost markets, the Fort Liberty E-6 example (BAH $2,100, estimated mortgage ~$1,600, positive monthly cash flow), and the PCS-to-rental-property strategy.

- [PCS Financial Planning: Month-by-Month Guide](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/pcs-financial-planning-guide): Month-by-month PCS financial checklist from orders drop through final voucher settlement. Covers DLA, MALT mileage (DTOD distance vs. GPS), per diem JTR calculation, TLE (14-day max, receipts required), PPM/DITY advance and settlement, VA loan pre-approval timeline (start 6 months out), and the common mistakes that leave $1,000–$5,000 on the table.

- [Dual Military Financial Strategies: Making Two Incomes Work](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/dual-military-financial-strategies): Financial mechanics for dual-active-duty couples — BAH co-location rules (senior with-dependents + junior without-dependents when co-located, vs. both with-dependents rates when geographically separated), two TSP accounts ($46,000 combined annual limit in 2026), two pensions (O-5 + E-8 example: $94,200/year combined at 20 years each), childcare cost impact ($2,000–$5,000/month off-CDC), and joint-spouse assignment request (JSAR) financial implications.

- [The OCONUS COLA Trap: Why Overseas Allowances Hurt Some Military Families](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/oconus-cola-trap): How OCONUS COLA (designed as a cost-of-living equalizer, not a bonus) becomes lifestyle inflation when service members spend it instead of saving it. Covers Yokosuka E-6 example ($700–$900/month COLA, $25,000–$32,400 over 3-year tour), three spend/save scenarios with 20-year compound growth, Roth TSP as the optimal COLA savings vehicle, and the same pattern for CONUS COLA in high-cost markets.

- [Best and Worst BAH Duty Stations in 2026](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/best-worst-bah-duty-stations-2026): Ranked analysis of BAH value by duty station — highest raw rates (San Francisco $5,127, NYC $5,070, Honolulu $3,663), lowest raw rates (Fort Leonard Wood $1,326, Fort Sill $1,479), and best-value markets by BAH surplus over actual housing costs (Fort Leonard Wood ~$476/month surplus, Fort Sill ~$529/month). Covers BAH rate protection rules and how to compare two duty stations for take-home pay.

- [Deployment Financial Planning: How to Bank $40,000+ on a Combat Tour](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/deployment-financial-planning): Systematic plan for maximizing the combat zone financial window — CZTE mechanics (enlisted: all pay excluded; officers: capped at E-9 max), Roth TSP triple tax advantage during CZTE months (tax-free contribution + tax-free growth + tax-free withdrawal), elevated TSP limit ($72,000 total additions vs. normal $24,500 elective deferral limit), Savings Deposit Program (10% guaranteed return on $10,000), Imminent Danger Pay ($225/month), and a full E-6 9-month tour model ($35,000–$50,000 realistic savings outcome).

- [2026 Military Pay Raise Explained: What 3.8% Actually Means for Your Paycheck](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/2026-military-pay-raise-explained): Breaks down the FY2026 3.8% pay raise (authorized Dec 18, 2025) in real dollar terms by grade — E-1 +$88/mo, E-5 +$150/mo, E-7 +$214/mo, O-3 +$283/mo, O-5 +$392/mo. Covers BAH increase (~4.2%), BAS increase (2.4%), DLA increase (3.8%), Family Separation Allowance increase to $300/month (first increase since 2002), historical context (5.2% in 2024, 4.5% in 2025, 3.8% in 2026), and what didn't change (TSP limits, SGLI rates). Uses exact FY2026 DFAS pay table figures throughout.

- [Military Credit Card Benefits: SCRA and MLA Fee Waivers Most Service Members Don't Know About](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/military-credit-card-scra-mla-benefits): Explains SCRA (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act) 6% interest cap on pre-service debt and how major banks (Chase, Amex, Citi, Capital One) voluntarily waive annual fees on premium cards worth $550–$695/year. MLA (Military Lending Act) caps MAPR at 36% for accounts opened during service. Covers how to claim benefits (call military benefits department, provide orders/LES), common mistakes (not knowing you qualify, canceling before separation, forgetting spouse applies independently), and separation timing strategy. Estimated household value: $2,400–$6,000+/year with $0 in fees.

- [TRICARE Costs in 2026: What You're Actually Paying vs. Civilian Health Insurance](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/tricare-costs-2026-vs-civilian): Active-duty TRICARE Prime costs $0 (no premiums, no deductibles at MTFs). Family coverage near-zero vs. civilian family plans at $600–$800/month premiums + $3,000–6,000 deductible. TRICARE Reserve Select: $57.88/month individual, $286.66/month family — saving Guard/Reserve members $14,560–$20,560/year vs. civilian employer plans. Retiree TRICARE and TRICARE For Life analysis. 2026 changes (pharmacy copay increases, TRS premium adjustment ~4–8%). Framework for counting healthcare in civilian job comparisons.

- [How to Read Your Military LES (Leave and Earnings Statement) in 2026](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/how-to-read-military-les-2026): Section-by-section guide to the Leave and Earnings Statement — Entitlements (BASEPAY, BAH, BAS, special pays, FSA), Deductions (FITW, FICA, SITW, SGLI, TSP, AFRH), Allotments, Summary, Leave balance (use-or-lose threshold at 60 days), YTD section, and Pay Entry Base Date (PEBD). Covers common errors: wrong dependency status (affects BAH), TSP contribution not set correctly (loses BRS matching), SGLI coverage at wrong level, state tax withholding for wrong state. Combat zone LES differences (FITW drops to zero for enlisted under CZTE).

- [SGLI vs. VGLI vs. Private Life Insurance: What Every Service Member Needs to Know](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/sgli-vgli-private-life-insurance): SGLI: $500,000 coverage at $30/month, guaranteed-issue regardless of occupation or health — terminates 120 days after separation. VGLI: guaranteed-issue conversion but premiums escalate every 5 years by age bracket ($43/month at 30–34, $107/month at 40–44, $399/month at 55–59 for $500K coverage). Private 20-year term: $25–35/month for a healthy 30-year-old, fixed rate for the term. Optimal strategy: buy private term 12–24 months before separation while still healthy. Combat zone exception: keep SGLI during deployment — private policies have war exclusion clauses. FSGLI for spouses up to $100,000. VGLI appropriate when health conditions make private underwriting unaffordable.

- [CRDP vs CRSC: Which One Pays More After Taxes?](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/crdp-vs-crsc-military-retirement): Most eligible military retirees with VA disability ratings don't realize they have a choice between CRDP and CRSC — and picking wrong can cost hundreds per month. Covers CRDP automatic restoration of full pension alongside VA pay (taxable), CRSC tax-free combat-related compensation, eligibility requirements for each, and the grade-by-grade math for determining which pays more after taxes.

- [The $47,000 Gap: Why Two E-5s With the Same Rank Make Wildly Different Money](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/the-47000-gap-bah-duty-station): Same rank, same years of service, nearly $47K/year difference in total compensation. Explains how duty station geography creates massive pay gaps through BAH variation ($1,260/month at Fort Sill vs. $3,726/month in Honolulu) and what that means for assignment preferences and civilian salary equivalents.

- [What Walking Away at 12 Years Actually Costs: The Retirement Math Nobody Shows You](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/what-walking-away-at-12-years-costs): An E-7 at 12 years is weighing whether to stay to 20. Quantifies the exact dollar value of the pension, TRICARE retiree healthcare, and TSP matching they'd forfeit — and calculates the civilian salary needed to replace it.

- [The Roth TSP Deployment Strategy That Builds a Tax-Free Fortune](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/roth-tsp-deployment-strategy): An E-5 who maxes Roth TSP during a 12-month combat deployment builds a tax-free asset worth six figures by retirement. Explains the combat zone triple tax advantage (contributions never taxed at any point), the elevated $72,000 TSP limit, and the full compound growth math through age 60.

- [50% + 30% + 20% = 100%, Right? How VA Math Actually Works (And What It Costs You)](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/va-math-costs-you-money): Most veterans expect their ratings to add up normally. They don't. Shows the step-by-step combined ratings formula explaining why 50% + 30% + 20% = 70% under VA math — and how targeting the right additional condition can push a combined rating to the next compensation tier.

- [The PCS That Costs $14,000 — And the One That Makes $6,000](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/pcs-that-costs-14000-vs-makes-6000): Two PCS scenarios for the same E-6 family moving Fort Campbell to JBLM. One loses thousands. The other profits. The $20,000 difference comes down to knowing DLA, TLE, PPM strategy, and lease timing before orders drop.

- [Dual Military BAH: Why the Higher-Ranking Spouse Doesn't Always Get More](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/dual-military-bah-guide): Most dual military couples assume the higher-ranking member should claim dependents for BAH. The math says otherwise — and it can cost you hundreds per month. Covers co-location rules, dependent assignment when stationed separately, and market-by-market optimization examples.

- [Your First Military Paycheck: What to Know Before You Spend It](https://www.milpaytools.com/blog/your-first-military-paycheck-what-to-know): What new service members need to understand before their first LES hits — BAH start date, TSP default enrollment, SGLI coverage, and the financial decisions that compound over a career.

## Data Sources

- 2026 Military Pay Tables: Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS)
- 2026 BAH Rates: Defense Travel Management Office (DTMO) official ASCII data download
- VA Disability Compensation Rates: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA.gov), effective December 1, 2025 (2.8% COLA)
- TSP Contribution Limits: Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and TSP.gov
- Healthcare Cost Benchmarks: KFF Employer Health Benefits Survey 2025, Healthcare.gov benchmark pricing
- TRICARE Premiums: TRICARE.mil, effective January 1, 2026

Built by Dan Stevens — grew up on Air Force bases worldwide as the son of a 20-year Air Force veteran, now an NMLS-licensed mortgage industry professional. 16 calculators, 34 blog posts, 7 comprehensive guides, 200+ BAH station pages, a transition financial roadmap, and a printable TAP student worksheet — all multi-LLM fact-checked against official government sources and verified with a Playwright test suite.
